title: pravapis transliteration scheme
description: A transliteration table (data/translit/*.yaml). NORMATIVE for any implementation. The table is consumed by a single left-to-right longest-match pass: at each position, the longest `from` whose condition holds is emitted and consumed, and the scan moves past it. That discipline is the point — a priority-ordered rule engine run to a fixpoint would let дз → dz be re-entered by з → z. Conditions are a closed vocabulary rather than regex so a scheme can be checked against a published table by someone who does not read code, and they are evaluated against the SOURCE string only, never against output already produced.

condition.description: A single context condition. Evaluated against the source string, with the matched grapheme spanning [start, end).

oneOf.title: source[start-1] is a vowel; ў counts as one
source[start-1] is a consonant (not a vowel, not ь/ъ)
source[end] is a vowel; ў counts as one
source[end] is one of е ё і ю я

when.description: One condition, or several joined by '|', meaning ANY of them (disjunction). There is no conjunction and no negation: a scheme that needs them is describing something this transducer should not be asked to do.

mapping.description: One grapheme, one output, one condition. Order matters only among mappings that share a `from`: the first whose condition holds wins. A longer `from` always beats a shorter one regardless of order.

from.description: The source grapheme. May be several characters (дзь, дж); longest match wins.

to.description: What it becomes. May be empty (a grapheme the scheme deliberately drops), several characters, or contain combining marks — compare as NFC.

lossy.description: The scheme has no faithful rendering for this grapheme; the output is a best effort and the caller is told via `unresolved`. A bare ь after a consonant with no soft Latin counterpart is the case in point. Reporting beats silently dropping.

scheme.description: The scheme's name. `lacinka` and `official` are the two shipped; a reverse table is named after the scheme it reads.

description.description: What the scheme is, and which orthography it pairs with. The pairing is not decoration: Łacinka marks assimilative softness exactly as Taraškievica does, the 2007 romanisation marks only the ь that is written, as Narkamaŭka does — so rendering converts to the paired orthography first.

source.description: The published table this one is transcribed from, cited well enough to check it against. Required: a transliteration scheme with no source is a preference.

reverse_of.description: Present on a Latin → Cyrillic table: the name of the forward scheme it inverts. A scheme that does not record assimilative softness has no faithful inverse and must NOT ship one — reading it back would be a guess about something the source never wrote down.

tests.description: Inline cases, exported verbatim into the conformance corpus.

x-constraints: Coverage: every letter of the scheme's source alphabet must be consumable by some mapping, or the scheme has a blind spot that will surface as `unresolved` on real text. Enforced by validate_scheme().
A mapping list must not contain two entries with the same (from, when) pair: the second can never be reached.
Conditions read the source string only. A mapping can never observe a decision another mapping already made.
